item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00475","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C23","C11","C14"],"selected_candidate_label":"C23","confidence":0.86,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C23 plausibly supplied the administrative framework adapted by the child: a government-wide program carried out within individual agencies, centrally directed and coordinated by the Bureau of the Budget, with periodic progress reports to the President. That combination is concrete and material, not merely a shared emergency topic or routine reporting clause. C11 and C14 also establish coordinated study programs, but their commission or interagency-committee machinery is less closely aligned with the child's Bureau-led, agency-executed structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The active direction of the program should be undertaken by the Bureau of the Budget, although the preparation of the studies themselves should be carried out by the individual agencies.","parent_excerpt":"Department and agency heads shall ... provide for periodic and systematic appraisals of operations ... [and] The Bureau of the Budget shall ... advise and assist the agencies in working out programs to improve their operations","explanation":"Both divide responsibility between agency-level execution and central Bureau of the Budget direction or assistance in a government-wide evaluative program."},{"child_excerpt":"I hope that you will report to me from time to time on the progress of the agencies in carrying forward the historical program.","parent_excerpt":"The Bureau of the Budget shall ... report periodically to the President on the progress and results of agency management improvement efforts.","explanation":"The child closely reproduces the Bureau's periodic presidential reporting role concerning agency progress."},{"child_excerpt":"I am confident that this program will be useful in improving operations.","parent_excerpt":"provide for periodic and systematic appraisals of operations to identify opportunities to improve effectiveness and performance","explanation":"The historical studies replace management appraisals as the evaluative instrument, while retaining improvement of agency operations as a central purpose."}]}
